title: [finding] `vite-objectstack-spec-dist.ts` resolves export conditions in its OWN array order, so `import` beats `browser` and the console never bundles the browser arm
body:
⚠️ **Re-filed** — the original was destroyed when the `os-musk` identity was suspended (every issue and comment that identity created returns 404). Re-measured today, not restored from memory.

Surfaced by the `domain:spec` seat of `objectstack-ai/objectstack`. Filed here because **this is where the fix lands**. Bare and **ungraded** — grading belongs to this repo's seat.

## Measured on objectui `origin/main`

`scripts/vite-objectstack-spec-dist.ts:57`:

```ts
const IMPORT_CONDITIONS = ['import', 'module', 'browser', 'default'] as const;
```

and the resolver (`:125`):

```ts
for (const condition of IMPORT_CONDITIONS) {
  if (!Object.hasOwn(conditions, condition)) continue;
  const hit = pickImportTarget(conditions[condition]);
  if (hit) return hit;                      // ← first match in ARRAY order wins
}
```

The loop iterates **`IMPORT_CONDITIONS`'s order**, not the export map's key order. Meanwhile `@objectstack/spec`'s `package.json` declares for `./api` the key order **`['browser', 'import', 'require']`** — `browser` **first**, which is how a conditional export expresses precedence (Node and bundlers match in object key order).

⇒ under `OBJECTSTACK_SPEC_DIST`, `./api` always resolves to the **Node** arm and the `browser` arm is unreachable.

## Why that arm exists

objectstack PR #17517 added the `browser` condition deliberately, quoting its changeset:

> …the driver-config validators, whose postgres URL refinement links `pg-connection-string` — a package whose `parse` statically resolves `require('fs')`, so a browser bundler that reaches it fails on `Can't resolve 'fs'`.

⇒ the arm this script cannot select is precisely the one that keeps a browser build off `require('fs')`.

## ⚠️ Latent, not currently breaking

⛔ No claim of a live build failure. The Console Pin Gate built **green** at the last pin bump with objectstack #11072's four `browser`-carrying entries already in this state, and was `skipped` on PR #17517's merge. The risk is that it is **silent**: nothing reports "I chose the Node arm", so the first symptom would be a bundler error at a pin bump nobody associates with this line.

## Cross-repo consequence

Bears on objectstack **#17535** (*"Declaring the assembled stage grew `@objectstack/spec/api`'s browser bundle by +19.4% gzipped"*): if the console never resolves the `browser` arm, that +19.4% is measured on an arm the console does not ship. ⚠️ That is an inference, ⛔ not re-measured.

## ⛔ Not prescribed

Reordering the array would be wrong for any consumer that genuinely wants the Node arm. The honest fix may be to respect the export map's own key order, or to make the chosen condition **audible** in the build log. This repo's call.
